sections.title: Stapled Security & Leverage
sections.subtitle: APA's own income and gearing measures

charts.title: Distribution vs Free Cash Flow per Security
charts.annotation: Both in cents per stapled security. FreeCashFlowPerSecurity is only disclosed from FY2022.

charts.title: Total Drawn Debt
charts.annotation: Total drawn debt is APA's own gearing figure (nets deferred borrowing costs and FX); it runs slightly above balance-sheet total debt.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For APA Group: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For APA Group: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

distributionPerSecurity.title: Distribution and free cash flow per security
distributionPerSecurity.content:
Distribution per security is the cash APA pays out per stapled security each period, in cents. Free cash flow per security is reported FCF divided by securities on issue.

For APA Group: APA is an income vehicle -- distributions have risen every year since FY2016 and are funded from cash flow, not statutory earnings, which is why this pairing matters more than EPS/DPS here. A distribution running above free cash flow per security signals it is being funded by debt rather than operations.

What to watch:

  • Distribution growth outrunning free cash flow per security growth
  • The payout's coverage ratio (FCF per security ÷ distribution per security) trending down

totalDrawnDebt.title: Total drawn debt
totalDrawnDebt.content:
Total drawn debt is APA's own leverage measure -- borrowings net of deferred borrowing costs and FX revaluation -- the figure it quotes when discussing gearing, shown against the raw balance-sheet total debt field for comparison.

For APA Group: APA is a highly-levered, capital-intensive pipeline operator running a large multi-year growth capex programme; drawn debt has grown from ~$9.0bn (FY2016) to over $14bn (FY2026) alongside that build-out. The DCF's net-debt bridge also grosses up APA's subordinated hybrid notes to 100% debt rather than the ratings agencies' 50% equity credit.

What to watch:

  • Drawn debt growth outpacing EBITDA growth (rising leverage multiple)
  • Refinancing walls and hybrid note reset/step-up dates in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For APA Group: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For APA Group: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For APA Group: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For APA Group: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For APA Group: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For APA Group: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For APA Group: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For APA Group: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
